set.body:
REPRODUCED, two probes differing only in statement order.

  ORDER A: touch WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.recallParaphrases FIRST, then WarOfTheGhostsModel.model
    -> ExceptionInInitializerError
    -> Caused by: IllegalStateException: War of the Ghosts fixture failed validation:
         [Error] claims.unique-ids @ claims/wog:claim:member:null:null: 2 claims share id
         [Error] claims.unique-ids @ claims/wog:claim:part:wog:sit:we-fought:Agent:null: 2 claims share id
         [Error] entity-relation.membership-acyclic @ entities/null: cyclic membership
         [Error] entity-relation.no-self @ entityRelations/0: self relation

  ORDER B: touch WarOfTheGhostsModel.model FIRST, then Expectations
    -> works. 71 situations, 10 paraphrases.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TEST-ORDER QUIRK: the error says THE FIXTURE IS INVALID. It names duplicate claim ids, a cyclic membership and a self relation. Every one of those is a lie - fixturesJVM is 114/114 green and the model validates fine when reached first. Anyone who writes a consumer that happens to touch Expectations first will be told their story model is corrupt, with four specific and entirely fictitious validation errors. I lost time to exactly that before working out it was ordering.

MECHANISM, stated as inference rather than proof. Expectations imports WarOfTheGhostsModel.{E, S} (WarOfTheGhostsExpectations.scala:13). Model does NOT reference Expectations - zero occurrences - so this is not a mutual dependency between the two files. The `null`s throughout the error are the signature of reading a val before its initializer has run, and S is a nested object inside WarOfTheGhostsModel. The consistent story is: forcing S from outside begins S's initialization, which triggers the enclosing object's initialization, which reads S.xxx while S is still initializing and gets null. I have NOT proved that; I have proved the order dependence and matched the null signature to it.

SUGGESTED FIX DIRECTION, not prescribed: make the dependency one-way at the value level as well as the file level - e.g. hoist the id objects (E, S) out of WarOfTheGhostsModel into their own top-level object that neither file's construction depends on. That removes the cycle rather than documenting it. A comment saying "touch Model first" is not a fix; nothing enforces it and the failure mode is a false validation report.

A CHEAP GUARD REGARDLESS OF THE FIX: one test that touches Expectations before Model and asserts the model loads. It is two lines and it fails today.

Found while measuring out-of-the-box alignment; not related to that work.
